title: Misery
text:
It was evening in Petersburg, and wet snow was falling. The cab driver Iona Potapov sat motionless on his sleigh, white with snow, his little mare equally still. That week his son had died, and he had not yet been able to talk about it to anyone.

An officer hired him. As they drove, Iona turned around and said, "My son, sir, died this week." "What did he die of?" asked the officer, and then told him to drive on and keep his eyes on the road. Later three noisy young men climbed in, arguing and cursing at him to go faster. Iona tried again to tell them about his son. One of them answered that we all must die, and told him to hurry up.

Iona looked at the crowds hurrying along the streets. Among all those thousands, was there not one who would listen? He went back to the cabmen's lodging house, where a young driver got up for a drink of water. Iona asked if he was thirsty and began, "My son died." But the young man had already covered his head and gone back to sleep.

It was too early to bed. Iona went out to the stable, where his mare stood munching hay. "Are you eating?" he asked her. "Suppose you had a foal, and that foal died. You would be sorry, would you not?" The mare munched and breathed on her master's hands. And Iona told her everything.
lesson: Someone grieving often needs nothing more than a person willing to listen. Take a moment to hear people out, even strangers.
